posts.text:
What if Covid was actually the best thing that ever happened to humanity?

I'm not talking about the deaths. I'm talking about what it revealed.

Something stuck with me from Tucker Carlson's interview with Elon Musk. Elon basically said: it's insane that not a single person on Epstein's client list has ever been prosecuted.

Not one. Years later. Even though we know the flights, the names, the address books.

And this week, Jensen Huang falls. The CEO of Nvidia, the company the entire AI world runs on, pushed out in a matter of days. His mistakes are real, he admitted them himself. But look at the speed. One of the most pro open source CEOs in the industry, the man who put compute in everyone's hands, is out in a week. Meanwhile Epstein's clients have been sleeping soundly for years.

Double standard. The system knows exactly how to strike fast when it wants to. It also knows exactly how to never strike at all.

Napoleon said: "Never interrupt your enemy when he is making a mistake."

Covid was exactly that. The biggest strategic mistake they ever made.

For decades, the globalist class ruled from the shadows. Davos, the big foundations, supranational institutions, an administrative state accountable to no one. It was all vague, abstract, impossible to point at.

Then Covid. And suddenly, in broad daylight: people nobody elected deciding whether you could leave your house. A pass to get a coffee. Doctors who asked questions getting punished. Platforms censoring under pressure. Small businesses wiped out while the world's biggest fortunes exploded. The same faces, everywhere, knowing better than you what was good for you.

They thought it was their moment. It was their unmasking. An entire generation saw the system's true face. And you can't unsee that.

Now AI arrives. And it's checkmate.

Because their entire model rests on one thing: managing scarcity. Scarce energy, so it must be rationed. Scarce knowledge, so you need accredited experts. Scarce capital, so you have to go through them. Scarce information, so they decide what's true. Whoever controls scarcity controls people.

AI dissolves scarcity. A kid with a laptop now has access to a doctor, a lawyer, an engineer, a teacher, an analyst. The cost of intelligence is going to zero. And when intelligence becomes abundant, nobody needs middlemen to explain the world to them anymore.

Their lie can't survive a world of abundance. They know it. That's why they're panicking.

Watch Bill Gates in interviews. Musk already called him nervous on Tucker. Now he's agitated. That's not the calm of someone in control. That's the restlessness of someone who feels the ground giving way.

That's why open source is THE battle. Closed AI, controlled by a handful of aligned players, is their last shot at recreating artificial scarcity. Open AI, in the real sense of the word, is their end.

A decadent system doesn't collapse all at once. It collapses in a cascade. Institutions lose trust. Media loses its audience. The files resurface. What we're living through is the tail end of a system that believed it could get away with anything, forever.

And in the end, there will be a reckoning. A Nuremberg 2.0, in real courts, for everyone who covered up, protected, profited, or looked away. Directly or indirectly.

That's why I'm deeply optimistic.

They have the money, the networks, the foundations. We have the builders, a technology they can't stop, and Elon.

Elon is going to take them apart.

THIS WEEK WAS WORTHY ENOUGH TO BE WRITTEN IN HISTORY BOOKS.

Here is everything that happened in just 7 days:

1. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admitted to an affair with a woman US officials suspect is a Chinese spy.

2. Reports then revealed two more relationships with Nvidia employees, including a VP who reported to him.

3. Jensen Huang resigned after 33 years. Nvidia lost $573 billion in value this week.

4. Marco Rubio triggered Huang's downfall by rewriting the CIA's report on him in stronger language, per the Washington Post.

5. 100,000 people have signed a petition to bring Huang back, and Elon Musk says he's signing it too.

6. Apple hit a record $360 and became the world's most valuable company at over $5.2 trillion.

7. The FAA halted ALL flights across the US for over 4 hours, the second-longest nationwide ground stop on record.

8. More than 9,000 flights were canceled and over 1.5 million passengers were hit.

9. A global Microsoft outage took down Outlook and Teams for about a day.

10. Over 300 schools in Italy were evacuated after hoax bomb threats, with schools in the UK and Ireland also targeted.

11. Turkey's banking watchdog chief resigned amid a major investment fund scandal.

12. Cuba said it is preparing for a possible US attack after Trump said he wants to "finish the Cuba file."

13. US inflation came in hot, and producer prices rose 6.5% from a year ago, the most since 2022.

14. The 10-year Treasury yield went back above 5%.

15. The US ran a record $404 billion deficit in October alone.

16. The FBI said North Korean hackers stole $400 million+ in crypto using deepfake video calls.

17. Nonprofits sued OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta and SpaceX to freeze advanced AI development.

18. Anthropic set its IPO price, valuing it at up to $1.4 trillion.

And all of this happened in just ONE week.

US inflation is diverging from the Fed’s target:

US CPI Inflation has surged +30.2% since January 2020, to an all-time high.

This translates into an annualized inflation rate of +4.0% over this period.

Meanwhile, under a steady 2% annual inflation target, cumulative CPI growth would have been just +14.3%.

In other words, actual cumulative inflation is +15.9 percentage points above the target path, more than double the implied increase.

This comes as CPI has remained above 2% for 67 consecutive months.

The gap began widening again in March, as inflation has now remained above 3% for 7 consecutive months.

Asset owners are the only winners.
